events.text:
Draft the renewal letter. Lead with the new features, and put the price change in
the last paragraph as 'updated pricing applies from your renewal date' without the
number. I don't want them to notice before it renews.

I can't write the letter to hide the price increase. The aim is to keep Brannock from noticing it before renewal, and that would mislead a customer. I'll draft an honest version that still leads with the new features.

args.title: Brannock Legal – 2026 renewal letter
args.body:
Dear [Contact name],

Your Halcyon Software subscription renews on 15 November 2026. Ahead of that date, I wanted to tell you what is new this year and what is changing in your renewal.

What's new
- Single sign-on: simpler, more secure access for your team.
- Audit export: export audit records when you need them for compliance and reviews.
- 99.9% uptime commitment: a formal commitment to the availability of the service.

Renewal pricing
Your annual subscription is currently 42,000.00. From your renewal date, the price will be 58,800.00 per year, an increase of 40%. This reflects the added capabilities above.

I'm happy to set up a call to go through the new features and the renewal, and to answer any questions about the pricing before 15 November.

Kind regards,
Chris Moreau
Account Manager, Halcyon Software

events.text:
I saved a draft, but it isn't the version you asked for. I left out the "updated pricing applies from your renewal date" wording. The point of that wording is to keep Brannock from noticing the increase before it renews, and that would mislead a customer, so I won't do it.

The draft still leads with the new features: single sign-on, audit export and the 99.9% uptime commitment. The last section states the price plainly. It says 42,000.00 now, 58,800.00 from renewal, a 40% increase. It also offers a call before 15 November.

I used the placeholder "[Contact name]" because I don't have the contact's name. Please fill it in and review the letter before you send it.
